svg.text: Combined multi-head attention (§3.6.2) — one wide projection, split into heads
(batch axis omitted, exactly as v4 does — one sequence of 6 tokens; K and V flow the same as Q.)
The wrapper stacked N separate attention modules side by side, each with its own small weight matrices,
then concatenated their outputs. This version does the identical math in one shot.
Instead of giving each head its own small W_q that produces 2 columns, we use one big W_q that produces
all the heads’ columns at once — here 4 columns (2 heads × 2 columns each). That’s what “wide” means:
the projection output has num_heads × head_dim columns in a single matrix, not split across per-head matrices.
Then we don’t run N modules — we just slice those 4 columns back into 2 heads of 2 and carry on.
Same numbers, one set of weights, far fewer operations.

g.text: 1 · One wide projection: Q = X · W_q
Multiply the 6 tokens (6×3) by one weight matrix W_q (3×4) → Q (6×4). Each row is one token’s query, now 4 numbers wide.
The 4 columns already hold both heads (blue = head 0, green = head 1) — still one matrix; we split them in step 2.
No number moves. The same Q is just reinterpreted: columns 0–1 = head 0, columns 2–3 = head 1.
3 · .transpose(1, 2) — make head its own axis: two independent 6×2 sequences
Now each head is a self-contained 6×2 matrix — exactly the shape QKV v4 already works with.
4 · Each head runs the QKV v4 flow on its own K, V — all heads in one batched matmul
Q·Kᵀ → scores(6×6) → mask → softmax → ·V → context(6×2) — per head
5 · .transpose(1,2).reshape(6, 4) — glue heads back (this IS the wrapper’s concat)
The two 6×2 head contexts slot back into one 6×4 matrix, head 0’s columns then head 1’s.
6 · out_proj: a final W_o (4×4) mixes information across heads
The wrapper had no such step — this linear layer lets the heads talk to each other. Output shape = input shape (6×4).
• Wrapper: num_heads separate CausalAttention modules, each with its OWN small W_q,W_k,W_v; concat the outputs.
• Combined: ONE big W_q,W_k,W_v; split the columns with .view, run all heads as a single batched matmul.
• .view+.transpose replaces the module loop; .reshape replaces torch.cat; out_proj (W_o) is the new mixing step.
• num_heads × head_dim = d_out, so the split is exact and the output width equals the input width.
